Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the TerraNova Energy Corp. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to TerraNova Energy Corp.'s Q2 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Steve Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Kline, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Strong operational performance in our generation fleet.
    2. Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
    3. Effective cost management.
    4. Progress on our infrastructure investments.
    5. Successful integration of the Haysi Energy Center.
    6. Advancement of our Clean Energy Future program.
    7. Positive regulatory outcomes in Georgia.

Let me provide some more detail on these seven key aspects. First, our generation fleet showed remarkable resilience, achieving high equivalent availability factors and commissioning new solar capacity ahead of schedule, even as we navigated weather disruptions and supply chain pressures. Second, renewables contributed significantly to growth, with new PPAs and higher dispatch rates bolstering our portfolio. Third, cost discipline kept O&M flat despite inflation, thanks to digital optimizations. Fourth, infrastructure investments in hardening and modernization reduced outage impacts substantially. Fifth, the Haysi Energy Center integration enhanced our PJM capacity auctions. Sixth, our Clean Energy Future program advanced decarbonization with CCUS pilots and storage deployments. And seventh, regulatory wins in Georgia provided timely rate relief.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Steve Harlan to discuss the financials.

Steve Harlan: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For the Q2 quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.33 and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Before moving further, let me dive deep into our revenue breakdown by regulated and unregulated segments, as this remains a focal point for investors amid volatile wholesale markets, surging data center loads, and supportive regulatory tailwinds from the Inflation Reduction Act. This balanced portfolio delivered resilient results, marking our 11th straight quarter of organic growth on a weather-normalized basis.

Regulated revenues came in at $1.92 billion, representing 67% of the total, up 6% year-over-year. These operations, centered on electric transmission and distribution in the Southeast through our Georgia and Florida subsidiaries and in the Midwest serving 2.8 million customers in MISO South, included $1.25 billion from retail electric sales. That grew 5% due to 2.5% higher residential usage from cooling demand and a 15% jump in commercial loads from hyperscale data centers in Atlanta and Columbus. Transmission added $450 million, supported by $1.2 billion in 345-kV line investments under the PJM RTEP cycle, yielding a 10.4% ROE on our $18 billion rate base. Weather-normalized retail sales rose 4.2%, in line with EIA Southeast cooling degree day projections. We captured $120 million in AFUDC on 500 MW battery storage projects in Florida nearing FERC approval by Q4. Our $300 million capex in AMI upgrades and DERMS supports EV integration, with 50,000 Level 2 chargers permitted in Florida. Rate cases progressed well: the Georgia filing for a $250 million annual increase at a 10.25% ROE is 80% settled, and we're advancing formula rates in MISO for a $2 billion five-year transmission plan. EBITDA margins held at 28%, with O&M flat year-over-year from Oracle CC&B productivity gains.

Unregulated revenues reached $930 million, or 33%, up 12% despite a 5% drop in average power prices to $43 per MWh. Across our 15 GW fleet—8 GW thermal, 4 GW renewables, and 3 GW storage/hydro—this included $520 million from merchant sales (56%), $280 million from renewables PPAs (30%), and $130 million from capacity and ancillaries (14%). ERCOT led with $375 million, up 25% on scarcity pricing during June heatwaves, where our 2 GW Corpus Christi peakers cleared 95% of high-price intervals above $500 per MWh. PJM contributed $250 million, aided by the 1.2 GW Haysi Energy Center securing BRA capacity at $240 per kW-year. Renewables in the Southwest delivered: $90 million from the 600 MW Lone Star Solar farm with a 15-year Google PPA at $35 per MWh, and Oklahoma wind at 38% capacity factor thanks to IRA PTC extensions. EBITDA margins expanded to 42% from 39% with 85% hedge cover at $42 per MWh above our $35 breakeven. Pacific Northwest hydro dipped 10% on low snowpack, costing $20 million, offset by 200 MW/800 MWh BESS at Chief Joseph. Forward curves indicate PJM 2025 LMPs at $38 per MWh, but AI demand may lift ERCOT peaks to $55 per MWh.

We're capitalizing on electrification trends, ramping unregulated capex to $1.5 billion annually for 2 GW solar-plus-storage by 2026, 70% pre-contracted to Microsoft and Meta. A CCUS pilot at our Indiana coal plant targets 45Q credits at $50 per ton CO2. This 55/45 regulated-unregulated mix supports 6-7% rate base CAGR and 15%+ unregulated EPS growth. We're tracking full-year regulated revenues of $7.8 billion and unregulated at $3.9 billion.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $1.15 billion, primarily focused on transmission upgrades and renewables. We remain committed to a strong balance sheet and shareholder returns. We anticipate narrowing full-year EPS guidance to $5.45 to $5.65.

To elaborate on that outlook, for Q3, we expect adjusted EPS of $1.28 to $1.38, up 5% at the midpoint from last year's $1.22. Drivers include 4-6% retail sales growth, led by 12-15% commercial/industrial from data center PPAs in PJM and ERCOT—over 1.2 GW contracted with hyperscalers. Renewables rise 20% quarter-over-quarter from our 2.5 GW solar-plus-storage, including 400 MW/1.6 GWh Desert Sun BESS at 28% capacity factors. CCGTs dispatch higher at 65-70%, nuclear at 93% post-upgrades. Offsets: O&M up 7-9% on labor and supply chains, interest up $0.08 per share. Regulated EBITDA $850-900 million, renewables/trading $120-140 million, corporate negative $30-40 million. Q3 capex $1.1-1.2 billion.

For full year 2024, we're raising to $5.45-$5.65 adjusted EPS, 6-9% above 2023's $5.18. Revenue $14.8-15.2 billion, EBITDA $4.95-5.15 billion up 7%, capex $4.6-4.8 billion including $1.8 billion regulated T&D, $1.2 billion renewables, $400 million modernization. Free cash flow $1.4-1.6 billion funds dividends and $500 million buybacks. Sensitivities: $0.50/MMBtu gas moves EPS $0.04, 1% sales $0.06. Assuming Fed cuts, net debt/EBITDA at 6.5x.

This embeds electrification, decarbonization, reliability megatrends—10 GW data center load in ERCOT, pumped hydro in PJM. Southeast rate base to $28 billion, Midwest wind repowers, Texas batteries. Risks like Ohio case lag, PTC cliffs, mitigated by hedges and CCUS.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Steve. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We're seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to advanced predictive maintenance, resulting in a 15% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

Building on that, let's discuss reliability metrics like SAIDI and SAIFI, and overall system performance. These drive customer satisfaction, rate case support, and clean energy funding. For full-year guidance into 2024, but reflecting Q2 trends, system-wide SAIDI was tracking at 84.2 customer-minutes, a 23% improvement from 2022's 109.5, beating our 95-minute target—our best since post-2018 Winter Storm Maya. SAIFI at 1.04, down 20% from 1.30, ahead of 1.15 target and 15-20% better than national averages of 102 minutes and 1.28.

Regionally: Northeast (Boston, Hartford) SAIDI 62.1 minutes, SAIFI 0.92 from undergrounding 15% overhead. Midwest (Illinois, Ohio) SAIDI 97.6 amid derechos, SAIFI 1.18 via 2.1 million miles vegetation management with LiDAR drones. Southwest (Arizona, Nevada) SAIDI 112.4 from heat/monsoons, SAIFI 1.32, 28% better sequentially; normalized under 70 excluding major events.

Three-year trends: SAIDI down 35%, SAIFI 27% from $1.2 billion grid hardening via our $450 million Grid Reliability Initiative. Pillars: GE Vernova GridOS ADMS on 85% feeders for FLISR, cutting restoration 22% (15 SAIDI minutes saved); AutoGrid AI forecasting 92% vegetation outages; 450 MW DER VPPs under FERC 2222; $250 million hardening, zero PSPS events.

This boosts NPS 14 points to 78, secures $800 million rate base adds, $15 million per 10 SAIDI minutes saved. 2024 guide: SAIDI 78-82, SAIFI 0.95-1.00 with $500 million more GRI, synchrophasors, EV orchestration. Risks from La Niña, transformers mitigated by buffers.

David Patel: Thank you, Maria. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the ERCOT market.

To share management's perspective on industry trends and challenges, we're in a transformative era with surging demand, fast decarbonization, and execution tests. Cautiously optimistic: fundamentals strong, but need discipline, innovation, regulatory sync.

Demand roars back: 2.5-3% annual U.S. growth to 2028 per EIA, ERCOT 5-7%, PJM peaks 166 GW up 15%. AI data centers, IRA EVs to 40% by 2030 adding 200 TWh, industrial reshoring 8% Midwest load growth.

Supply: 32 GW solar/wind 2023, renewables 43%; 10 GW BESS up 150%, e.g., NextEra Manatee. Offshore wind like Hornsea 3, China solar LCOE <$30/MWh.

Challenges: 2,300 GW queues, 4-5 year studies despite FERC 2023—20% of our 1.2 GW deprioritized. Supply chains: transformers 120-150 weeks, capex +15-25%. Aging infra: 70% lines >25 years, 1.5 million MWh curtailments. Rates at 4.2% yields compress ROE to 9.5%; weather $5B Florida losses; cyber up 25%.

Regional: PJM/MISO capacity gaps favor our 2.4 GW gas at 85%; ERCOT renewables 12 GW YTD; CAISO gas retirements; WECC hydro/drought; Europe REPowerEU.

Positioning: $1.8 billion of $4.2 billion 2024 capex to clean—600 MW BESS PJM, 400 MW H2-ready CCGT, Keystone CCUS 1 MtCO2/year $85/ton 45Q. ABB Ability predictive maintenance 15% O&M save, Fluence AI dispatch +25% ancillaries.

Tailwinds like $370B IRA create $1T opportunities to 2030. Diversified fleet—45% renewables, 30% nuclear/gas, 25% storage—ROIC >8%. Reliability first, growth second, sustainability always.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed Dragos Platform to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting GridOS ADMS in PJM territory.

Expanding on grid modernization and smart grid initiatives, facing decarbonization, DER growth, 1.2M annual EV registrations, $150B outage costs, our $1.2 billion three-year capex (15% total) yields 3.5x NPV, >12% IRR via efficiencies, revenues.

AMI at 92% of 2.5M endpoints cuts disputes 28%, dynamic pricing $45M revenue. Oracle Flex ADMS + GE GridOS slashes SAIDI 22% to 85 minutes, SAIFI 18% to 0.9 vs. EEI averages. DERMS on 75% footprint manages 450 MW solar/storage, IEEE 1547 inverters, 85% FERC 2222 VPPs.

Regional: Northeast PJM $250M urban microgrids, Siemens controllers restore <2 min. ERCOT VVO/CVR shaves 4-6% peaks, $18M savings, 2.5% energy save. Australia 100% AMI for NEM 50 GW renewables.

IRA $13B grants: $180M ITC/PTC for 200 MW behind-meter storage. NERC CIP v6 100%, Dragos mitigated 14 events. $400M O&M synergies by 2026, 35% transformer fails down. Enables hyperscaler integration.

This moat drives 15-20% ROE uplift, $10B ancillaries market by 2030.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our rate case filing in Georgia. This will allow us to recover $285 million.

Detailing updates on rate case filings and outcomes across Midwest/Plains like MPSC, KCC, PUCT—critical for $4.2B five-year capex, 40% clean/grid resiliency.

MPSC Dec order: $285M increase on $8.7B base (92% of $310M ask), full 10.0% ROE (up 25 bps), full $450M AFUDC on 600 MW wind incl. Prairie Winds III/NextEra, renewable rider decoupling.

Kansas KCC Q1: $210M on $6.2B (88% of $240M), ROE 9.75% but full MYRP three-year adjustments, trackers for $300M BESS (100 MW/400 MWh Flint Hills, DOE loan), $75M EV chargers.

Texas PUCT interim April: on track $420M on $12.5B for 2.1M customers, PBR with 20 bps ROE tie to demand response (1.2 GW summer), DER VPPs with Enphase.

Pending: Oklahoma OCC $520M on $14.3B for $1.2B modernization (Siemens ADMS, PMUs), Q4 hearing, 10.25% ROE post BB+ upgrade. Iowa formula $150M for nuclear uprates.

90% recovery last 24 months across eight dockets, $0.45 EPS accretion. Decarb riders cover 65% $1.8B renewables (1.2 GW solar-storage/Ørsted, 500 MW H2 blend). MYRPs year-end for 95% recovery, 6-8% EPS to 2028.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Steve, Maria, David, Lisa, and Robert. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for data center load growth and how it fits into revenue trends?

Johnathan Hale: Certainly. Data centers are a major tailwind, with hyperscalers driving 12-15% commercial growth in Q3 guidance and beyond. We've contracted 1.2 GW firm load, contributing to unregulated upside in ERCOT and PJM, aligning with 2.5-3% overall demand surge per EIA. This bolsters our renewables dispatch and merchant margins, as seen in Q2's 12% unregulated revenue growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Reynolds with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Reynolds: What is your outlook for full-year earnings and any updates to guidance?

Steve Harlan: Our narrowed FY24 adjusted EPS is $5.45-$5.65, reflecting strong H1 at $2.65, with Q4 $1.75-$1.85. Key is 5% retail sales, 15% renewables EBITDA to $750M, capex $4.6-4.8B. Sensitivities remain modest, and we're positioned for 6-8% CAGR through 2028 amid load growth and IRA benefits.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to weather and reliability metrics?

Maria Gonzalez: We're proactive with our Grid Reliability Initiative, delivering 23% SAIDI improvement to 84.2 minutes and 20% SAIFI drop to 1.04. Investments in ADMS, AI forecasting, VPPs, and hardening cut restoration times 22%, with normalized SAIDI under 70 excluding majors. 2024 targets 78-82 SAIDI amid La Niña, supported by inventory and partners.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Vargas with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Vargas: What is the anticipated impact of recent rate case outcomes on your earnings?

Robert Kline: Outcomes like MPSC's $285M at 10% ROE and Kansas MYRP deliver $0.45 EPS accretion from 90% recovery across dockets. Pending Oklahoma $520M and Texas PBR position us for 95% capex recovery, de-risking 6-8% growth even with softening wholesale prices.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q2, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning TerraNova Energy Corp. for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in TerraNova Energy Corp.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
